questions.q: What is a Business Service, as CSDM defines it?
options: A specific database server CI
A random collection of unrelated CIs
A relationship type used only in impact analysis
A service as the business or customer recognizes it, defined by the outcome it provides rather than the technology underneath
questions.explain: A Business Service is defined by business outcome — something like "Payroll" or "Email" that a non-technical stakeholder would recognize by name.

questions.q: What is a Technical Service, as CSDM defines it?
options: The underlying technical capability that delivers a Business Service, built from real CIs
A synonym for Business Service with no real difference
A report that lists all open Incidents
A location record used to group CIs by data center
questions.explain: The Technical Service is where the actual CIs and relationships live — the application stack, servers, and databases that make the Business Service work.

questions.q: What is the correct dependency direction between a Business Service, a Technical Service, and CIs?
options: CIs depend on the Business Service, which depends on the Technical Service
A Business Service depends on one or more Technical Services, which are built from, and depend on, individual CIs
There is no dependency direction — all three are modeled as unrelated records
A Technical Service depends on the Business Service it belongs to
questions.explain: The chain runs Business Service -> Technical Service -> CIs, which is what lets an outage be described correctly at any level.

questions.q: Why does this Business Service / Technical Service split matter for impact analysis?
options: It has no effect on impact analysis at all
It removes the need to maintain any CI relationships
It lets the same underlying fact be described correctly at the right altitude for whoever's asking — a CI-level answer for a DBA, a Business Service-level answer for a VP
It means only Technical Services can ever be reported as degraded
questions.explain: Without the split, impact analysis stays accurate but stuck at the technical level, which is meaningless to most decision-makers.

questions.q: Which of the following would most likely be modeled as a Business Service rather than a Technical Service?
options: A specific mailbox database CI
"Customer Portal," a name a non-technical stakeholder would recognize and care about directly
A relationship record linking a server to a database
A single application server instance
questions.explain: A Business Service is recognized by name and outcome by non-technical stakeholders; the mailbox database and application server are CIs underneath a Technical Service.
